focus: Template selection modal subject preview (in candidate messages tab)

test_scenarios.description: Navigate to a candidate's messages tab
test_scenarios.details: Navigated to /jobs/15819/stages/110706/applicants/12137/messages for candidate Lincoln McDermott. Messages tab loads with Subject field, message body editor, 'Send message' and 'Use template' buttons visible.

test_scenarios.description: Click 'Use template' to open the template selection modal
test_scenarios.notes: Required workaround: the 'Use template' button has type='submit' on a form, so clicking it via Playwright triggers a form submit and the SPA routes away. Had to use JavaScript evaluate to change button type to 'button' before clicking. The modal 'Choose template' opened successfully with title, description, template dropdown, Select/Cancel buttons.

test_scenarios.description: Select a template and verify the preview shows 'Subject: {rendered subject}' above the body preview
test_scenarios.details: Selected 'Thank you for applying' template from dropdown. Modal preview area appeared with: (1) Subject line: 'Subject: Software Engineer at Acme Inc.' rendered above the body preview, separated by a border-bottom. (2) Body preview showing template text with raw {{variables}} ({{CandidateFirstName}}, {{OrganizationName}}, {{JobTitle}}, {{SenderFullName}}).

test_scenarios.description: Verify the subject is rendered with actual candidate/job values (not {{variables}})
test_scenarios.details: The subject preview shows 'Subject: Software Engineer at Acme Inc.' — {{JobTitle}} resolved to 'Software Engineer' and {{OrganizationName}} resolved to 'Acme Inc.' The backend render_template_message method (job_application.rb:806) uses Mustache.render with placeholder_options to produce subject_raw, which the frontend displays via mailMerge.subjectRaw. Note: the body preview intentionally shows raw {{variables}} via template_html (uses placeholder_options_with_spans_unfilled), while the subject preview shows the fully rendered value.

test_scenarios.description: Click 'Use this template' (Select button) and verify the composer's subject field updates with the rendered subject
test_scenarios.details: Clicked 'Select' button. Modal closed. Composer now shows: Subject field = 'Software Engineer at Acme Inc.' and body = rendered template with actual values ('Hi Lincoln,' 'Software Engineer position', 'Rezu May'). The handleInsertTemplate function (ChannelMessageNew.tsx:50-56) sets the subject from mailMerge.subjectRaw. Note: the subject value is identical to the default subject (both resolve to 'Software Engineer at Acme Inc.'), so this test cannot distinguish whether the template subject was actually applied vs. the default remaining unchanged. A template with a custom/different subject would be needed to fully verify this.

test_scenarios.description: Take screenshots of the modal with subject preview visible
test_scenarios.details: Screenshots captured at each stage. Key screenshots: 04-choose-template-dropdown-open.png (dropdown with 3 templates), 05-template-selected-with-subject-preview.png (modal showing subject preview and body preview).

findings.title: Invalid CSS in SubjectPreview styled component — font-size uses full CSS declaration utility
findings.description: In ChannelMessageTemplateSelectionModal.tsx line 207, `font-size: ${t.text.sm};` produces invalid CSS because t.text.sm is a complete CSS declaration (includes 'font-size:' property already). This results in 'font-size: font-size: 0.875rem;' which is invalid. The subject preview text may not have the intended font size.
findings.status: KNOWN — documented in pipeline CLAUDE.md Known Failure Pattern #1

findings.title: Default templates all use same subject as the default composer subject, making template subject insertion hard to verify
findings.description: All 3 default templates ('Thank you for applying', 'Scheduling', 'Rejection') appear to use {{JobTitle}} at {{OrganizationName}} as their subject, which is the same as the default composer subject. When selecting a template, the subject field value doesn't visibly change, making it impossible to verify via UI testing alone that the template's subject was actually applied. A template with a distinct custom subject would be needed to fully verify the subject insertion flow.
findings.impact: If the template subject insertion code (handleInsertTemplate, line 53-55) were broken, the default would mask the bug because the value is the same.

findings.title: Body preview shows raw {{variables}} while subject preview shows rendered values — inconsistent rendering
findings.description: In the template selection modal preview, the subject shows fully rendered values ('Software Engineer at Acme Inc.') while the body shows raw template variables ({{CandidateFirstName}}, {{OrganizationName}}). This is by design: subject uses mailMerge.subjectRaw (Mustache-rendered with actual values) and body uses mailMerge.templateHtml (rendered with placeholder_options_with_spans_unfilled, which preserves variable markers). However, this inconsistency may confuse users — if the subject shows real values, users might expect the body preview to also show real values.
findings.backend_code: job_application.rb lines 801-808 — subject_raw uses placeholder_options (real values), template_html uses placeholder_options_with_spans_unfilled (preserves variables)

findings.title: 'Use template' button has type='submit' causing form submission and navigation away from messages tab
findings.description: The 'Use template' button in ChannelMessageNew.tsx (line 194-204) has type='submit' and form='channel-message-form'. Clicking it triggers both the onClick handler (which opens the template modal) AND a form submit event. The form submit causes the SPA to navigate away from the messages tab (typically to the overview or settings page). The modal does appear briefly but the underlying page changes. In automated testing, this required a JavaScript workaround to change button type before clicking. Users may also experience the page jumping when clicking 'Use template', though the modal overlay may mask this.
findings.fix: Change the 'Use template' button type from 'submit' to 'button', or remove the form attribute, since it uses onClick (onClickInsertTemplate) which calls event.preventDefault() — but the form submit still fires if the click handler doesn't fully prevent it.

summary: The template selection modal subject preview feature works correctly. When a template is selected in the 'Choose template' modal, the subject preview ('Subject: Software Engineer at Acme Inc.') appears above the body preview with the subject rendered using actual candidate/job values. Clicking 'Select' inserts both the rendered body and subject into the composer. Four findings were identified: (1) a known CSS bug in SubjectPreview, (2) a test gap where default template subjects match the default composer subject, (3) an inconsistency between subject rendering (real values) and body rendering (raw variables) in the preview, and (4) the 'Use template' button having type='submit' which causes form submission and page navigation.
